observations: Photo 0 shows a pile of multiple used automotive engine/transmission mounts, varying shapes and sizes, stacked on a wooden shelf.
Mounts show heavy rust, surface corrosion, and oxidation on metal brackets.
Rubber bushings visible in some mounts appear aged, some discolored, cracking not clearly visible due to angle/lighting.
A watermark 'POSTED ON KINGSLEY IBEH' overlays the image.
No brand, part number, or vehicle-specific marking is legible on any mount.
Items appear to be a mixed lot, not a single matched set for one vehicle.

claims.evidence: No shipping documents, container, or origin marking visible in photo 0.

claims.claim: Tested and working, no knock, low mileage, never opened
claims.evidence: Engine mounts have no 'knock' or 'mileage' characteristic; this claim appears to be mismatched/templated language, likely copied from an engine listing rather than describing mounts. Cannot be verified from a static photo.

risks.risk: Rubber bushing condition (cracked, perished, or separated from metal) which determines usable life
risks.proof: Close-up photos of each mount's rubber bushing from multiple angles, plus a flex/press test clip

risks.risk: Vehicle-specific fitment unknown; mounts vary by make/model and price depends heavily on this
risks.proof: Seller must specify or show a tag/stamp indicating which car model(s) each mount fits
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced without fitment confirmation

risks.risk: Rust extent may indicate long outdoor storage affecting structural integrity of brackets
risks.proof: Close-up of bracket metal showing any pitting or weakening, plus flex test

risks.risk: Lot composition and count (how many mounts, which types) unclear
risks.proof: A photo with each mount separated and labeled, plus itemized count
risks.if_unproven: priced as a single unverified mixed-lot unit

proof_requests: Specify the exact vehicle make, model, and year each mount is intended for
Close-up photos of each distinct mount showing rubber bushing condition
Any part number or OEM stamp visible on the mounts
A video showing the mount being flexed/pressed to demonstrate rubber integrity
response.reason: The lot contains multiple unidentified, non-vehicle-specific engine mounts with no readable part number or fitment marking, so even a worst-case price cannot be assigned until the buyer knows which vehicle(s) they fit and the true condition of the rubber bushings.
